page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.8-128 is a virtual machine configuration within the Standard family. It is provisioned with 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance offers dedicated CPU resource allocation with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, providing an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not come with integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, having zero GPUs. Persistent storage and data volumes must be provisioned via external network-attached block storage services. Because all baseline benchmarks for this instance profile report no data available, performance characteristics must be evaluated directly from its hardware specifications.

With an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.8-128 provides strong qualitative resource density for memory-bound applications without the expense of over-provisioning compute cores. The dedicated 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon cores suit workloads requiring consistent single-thread execution alongside substantial memory capacity. Primary use cases include in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, enterprise resource planning applications, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
